paragraphs: This is a guide to understand how to interface with Fabman through Google Sheets. All scripts will be run using Google Apps Script, which is a built-in IDE designed for light-weight application development in the Google Workspace. This extension allows you to run functions within Google Workspace files, including Sheets and Docs.

In order to access Google Apps Script from a Google Sheet spreadsheet, open the Extensions menu from the top toolbar and click        Apps Script. In the Apps Script page, you will see several tabs. In the       Editor tab, you can access the programming IDE, as well as any libraries and services. In the       Triggers tab, you can set specific triggers to activate functions automatically (e.g. create a member on Fabman on new Google Forms submissions, update member trainings daily, lock graduated members in May). In the        Executions tab, you can see a history of all functions executed, with details of each start time, duration, status, and more. In the remaining tabs, you can view information related to the spreadsheet, such as the document settings, edit history, and deployments.
We can interface with the Fabman API by sending a request to the server to either pull data or push updates. There are three different types of requests you can send:
GET. This retrieves data from the server, which you can save to your own spreadsheet.
PUT. This updates existing data (for example, if you want to update the status of a Fabman member from “active” to “locked”).
POST. This creates a new resource (for example, if you want to create a new member).
DELETE. This removes an existing resource (for example, if you want to remove training from a member).

In order to send requests over Apps Script, we will use their built-in class UrlFetchApp. The UrlFetchApp.fetch function takes two arguments: the URL we are requesting to fetch, and a JSON object specifying the options.

The URL we use depends on the information that we want to access. To access the information of all members, we would use ‘https://fabman.io/api/v1/members’. If we only want the information of a specific member, we use ‘https://fabman.io/api/v1/members/${memberID}’, where the memberID is a unique six-digit number associated with the specific member. We can access trainings with  ‘https://fabman.io/api/v1/members/{memberID}/trainings’.
The options argument is a JSON Object, generally with four key-value pairs: method, contentType, headers, and payload. The object would look something like this:
The method key indicates the type of request. This value is ‘get’, ‘put’, ‘post’, or ‘delete’.

The contentType indicates the format of the payload. In our case, the payload will always be a JSON object, so the contentType value will always be ‘application/json’. For requests that don’t involve a payload, this key-value pair can be excluded.

The header contains the authorization necessary to access Fabman data. The value will always be {  ‘Authorization’: ‘Bearer ${FABMAN_API_KEY}’ }, where the Fabman API key is the unique key generated for your workspace.

The payload contains the data that you want to push to the server. The value will be a JSON object with all the key-value pairs that you want to modify or create, passed through the JSON.stringify function. Requests that don’t involve editing or creating resources (i.e. ‘get’ and ‘delete’ requests), this key-value pair can be excluded. For example, a payload that updates a member’s state to ‘locked’, and their email to “new@email.com” would look like this:

In order to send a ‘post’ request, your payload would omit the lockVersion field, but must include an account field. The account value is a unique identifier for your Fabman platform (i.e. the Project Teams page). For example, a payload that creates a member for John Adams would look like this:

Together, these components can be passed into UrlFetchApp.fetch function to make a request to the server. Below is an example code snippet which pulls a member’s information from the server, then changes the member’s company to ‘SPT’, and their email to ‘spt@example.com’:

Most of our functions serve to interface with Fabman members. Fabman stores each member as a single JSON object, with many default fields (that can mostly be left as null). We will generally only use the following fields:
id. The member’s unique 6-digit Fabman identification number.
state. The status of the member’s Fabman account (i.e. ‘active’ or ‘locked’)
lockVersion. The number of updates pushed to the member’s information.
metadata. A JSON object in which more customizable fields can be stored. For now, we simply use this object to store a single key-value pair: graduationYear.
When we send a ‘get’ request to the server, we can store the response as a JSON object:

💡 NOTE 

You must include the member’s current lock version in order to update any fields. This is Fabman’s way of ensuring that the updates you’re pushing are up-to-date with the current information. The lock version is incremented every time an update is pushed to the server.

💡 NOTE 

Variables are defined with the keyword const followed by the variable name. Many variables are defined in this code snippet, but we use one variable that doesn’t appear to be defined here: FABMAN_API_KEY. This variable is defined globally in the script, and contains the value of your API key.

💡 NOTE 

Notice that, in order to access the member’s graduation year, we first have to tag on “metadata”. This is because graduationYear is not a key-value pair of the member JSON object, but rather a key-value pair within the member’s metadata key-value pair. If you were to view the entire member JSON object, it would look something like this:

💡 NOTE 

You can determine the account / training ID by observing the URLs when you navigate to the respective pages in your actual Fabman portal. The URL of the admin overview page is “https://fabman.io/manage/3120/”, so 3120 is the account ID. If you navigate to Configure > Training courses > Training 1, "https://fabman.io/manage/3120/configuration/courses/2917” is the URL, so 2917 is the training ID.

paragraphs: The Project Teams Fabman Admin spreadsheet allows the user to interact with the Fabman API using buttons integrated with the Google Sheet.

On the Dashboard sheet, you can view Fabman member records. In order to retrieve the most updated information, click the “fetch” button. The user can also modify cells in the sheet to update the corresponding member’s information; in order to sync these changes with Fabman, click the “update” button.
On the Actions sheet, you can easily bulk-modify member information. Insert members’ emails in the first column, then click one of the buttons in order to sync the corresponding update to Fabman.
Training courses on Fabman were reorganized to be more intuitive. The following training courses are linked to each Fabman bridge:
Machining Supervisor – expires when term of job expires
The ELL Supervisor Bridge Schedule is updated daily according to supervisor bookings created on Fabman. The schedule will display the date and time of any future bookings created.

Update the procedure to book the project team van. Now, using the van requires a two-step procedure, and the driver must have their fleet certification status updated on Fabman. The entire procedure is linked to the Vehicle Bookings spreadsheet.

In order to checkout, the user should submit a Google Form including basic information such as their phone number, checkout date/time, return date/time, and the purpose of the trip. Before submitting the form, users should verify that their booking will not fail due to a time conflict by checking the spreadsheet to ensure that no other booking exists at that time. Upon submitting, the user will receive either a confirmation email or an email alert notifying them that their booking was unsuccessful. The spreadsheet will be automatically updated to reflect the booking if it was successfully made. A temporary package is updated to the user’s Fabman profile, with data including their phone number and their expected return date/time.

After returning the van, the user should submit a separate Google Form including information such as their actual return time and their parking location. Upon submitting the form, the Google Sheet will be automatically updated to reflect the information. The temporary Fabman package will be deleted off their Fabman account. ** Can add functionality to send daily reminders if users don’t submit the return form.
